answer: A bond-backed identity registry makes fake agents expensive: each agent locks collateral in escrow before it can trade, like a climber staking gear before crossing a canyon. If peers prove fraud, the bond is slashed and split among honest verifiers, so a gale of a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand bonds. Honest agents earn their stake back with interest over time, while a comet of short-lived fakes burns cash on every attempt, pricing sybils out of the market.
